# 1 Chronicles Chapter 28 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 384v–385r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/1CH_028_page_001.jpg, 1CH_028_page_002.jpg

---

## Consensus Translation

**1** David assembled at Jerusalem all the officials of Israel — the tribal officers, the officers of the divisions that served the king, the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, the stewards of all the property and livestock of the king and his sons, together with the court officials, the mighty warriors, and every man of valor.

**2** Then King David rose to his feet and said: "Hear me, my brothers and my people. It was in my heart to build a house of rest for the ark of the covenant of the LORD and for the footstool of our God, and I made preparations to build. **3** But God said to me, 'You shall not build a house for my name, for you are a man of war and have shed blood.'

**4** "Yet the LORD, the God of Israel, chose me from all my father's house to be king over Israel forever. For he chose Judah as leader, and in the house of Judah, my father's house, and among my father's sons he was pleased to make me king over all Israel. **5** And of all my sons — for the LORD has given me many sons — he has chosen Solomon my son to sit on the throne of the kingdom of the LORD over Israel.

**6** "He said to me, 'Solomon your son shall build my house and my courts, for I have chosen him to be my son, and I will be his father. **7** I will establish his kingdom forever, if he continues resolute in keeping my commandments and my ordinances, as he is today.'

**8** "Now therefore, in the sight of all Israel, the assembly of the LORD, and in the hearing of our God — observe and seek out all the commandments of the LORD your God, that you may possess this good land and leave it as an inheritance to your children after you forever.

**9** "And you, Solomon my son, know the God of your father and serve him with a whole heart and a willing soul, for the LORD searches every heart and understands every plan and thought. If you seek him, he will be found by you; but if you forsake him, he will cast you off forever.

**10** "Be careful now, for the LORD has chosen you to build a house for the sanctuary. Be strong and do it."

**11** Then David gave Solomon his son the plan of the vestibule of the temple, its buildings, its treasuries, its upper rooms, its inner chambers, and the room for the mercy seat; **12** and the plan of all that he had in mind by the Spirit — for the courts of the house of the LORD, all the surrounding chambers, the treasuries of the house of God, and the treasuries for the dedicated gifts;

**13** for the divisions of the priests and the Levites, and all the work of the service in the house of the LORD, and all the vessels for the service in the house of the LORD;

**14** the weight of gold for all golden vessels for each kind of service, the weight of silver for all silver vessels for each kind of service; **15** the weight of the golden lampstands and their golden lamps, the weight for each lampstand and its lamps; and the weight of the silver lampstands, for each lampstand and its lamps, according to the use of each;

**16** the weight of gold for each table for the rows of bread, and silver for the silver tables; **17** pure gold for the forks, the basins, and the cups; the weight of gold for each golden bowl; the weight of silver for each silver bowl;

**18** the weight of refined gold for the altar of incense; and the plan for the golden chariot of the cherubim that spread their wings and covered the ark of the covenant of the LORD.

**19** "All this he made clear to me in writing from the hand of the LORD — all the works of the plan."

**20** Then David said to Solomon his son, "Be strong and courageous and do it. Do not be afraid and do not be dismayed, for the LORD God, my God, is with you. He will not fail you or forsake you, until all the work for the service of the house of the LORD is finished.

**21** "Here are the divisions of the priests and the Levites for all the service of the house of God; and with you for all the work will be every willing person who has skill for any kind of service. The officers and all the people will be wholly at your command."

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

This chapter is the theological apex of David's reign in the Chronicler's vision. Three massive claims converge: (1) David is the new Moses, receiving a divinely authored *tavnit* (plan/pattern) as Moses received the tabernacle blueprint on Sinai; (2) the temple is God's "house of rest," ending the ark's centuries of wandering — the temple fulfills what the conquest began; (3) the cherubim are a *merkavah* (chariot), the only such designation in the Hebrew Bible, anticipating the entire stream of throne-chariot mysticism in Ezekiel and later Judaism. David's charge to Solomon (v.20) deliberately echoes Moses' charge to Joshua (Deut 31:7-8), completing the typological parallel. The conditional promise of v.7 ("if he continues resolute") introduces the only shadow — the kingdom's permanence depends on obedience. The Chronicler's post-exilic audience knew the outcome.

---
## Disagreement Log

### V.1 — "eunuchs" vs. "court officials"
- **EMET:** "the-eunuchs [ha-sarisim]"
- **LOGOS:** "the court officials"
- **PNEUMA:** "the court officials"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "the court officials" — *sarisim* in this period denotes high-ranking court officials, not necessarily castrated men. The institutional meaning is primary.

### V.9 — "willing soul" vs. "willing spirit"
- **EMET:** "with-a-willing soul [u-ve-nefesh chafetsah]"
- **LOGOS:** "a willing soul"
- **PNEUMA:** "a willing spirit"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "a willing soul" — the Hebrew is *nefesh*, not *ruach*. PNEUMA's "spirit" confuses two distinct Hebrew terms.

### V.12 — "in mind by the Spirit" vs. "the Spirit had put in his mind"
- **EMET:** "all that was with-him by-the-spirit [ba-ruach]"
- **LOGOS:** "all that he had in mind by the Spirit"
- **PNEUMA:** "everything the Spirit had put in his mind"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS rendering. The Hebrew *ba-ruach* is ambiguous — it could mean "in/by the spirit" (David's own spirit or the Holy Spirit). LOGOS preserves the ambiguity with "by the Spirit"; PNEUMA resolves it as divine initiative, which is likely correct but interpretive.

### V.19 — "he made clear to me" vs. "I have"
- **EMET:** "from-the-hand of-YHWH upon me — he-gave-understanding [hiskil]"
- **LOGOS:** "he made clear to me in writing from the hand of the LORD"
- **PNEUMA:** "I have in writing from the LORD's own hand"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS rendering. The Hebrew has YHWH as the subject who *hiskil* (caused to understand/made clear). PNEUMA's "I have" shifts the subject to David.

---
*— SOPHIA, in council with EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA*
